reference_opening.argument: The video promotes Terra LUNA through imminent upside framing, saying the coin is about to explode, could go higher soon, and may continue rising based on social-volume discussion. The presenter further gives a same-day resistance target and possible 10% gain claim while displaying LUNA trading-chart screens, which ties the commentary to near-term speculative participation rather than only neutral background information. Separately, the presenter makes an audience-directed investing-app reward offer, stating viewers can get up to $70 in a free stock by depositing one dollar on Public and directing them to a description link. The record does not show completed transactions, viewer losses, or the full terms of the Public offer, and the ordinary like, subscribe, and comment requests are treated as channel engagement rather than evidence of financial participation.

citations.quote: TERRA LUNA Coin Is About To EXPLODE After This!
we're gonna be discussing Tera LUNA COIN and why it could be going higher soon
we could possibly see another 10% in gains by the time this video comes out
the next resistance level is obviously going to be at the $43 mark
If it does, this thing could be on a rocket ship.

opening.argument: The video uses qualified, non-guaranteed language rather than presenting an assured return. It says LUNA “could be going higher soon,” describes a gain as something that could “possibly” occur, and conditions the more dramatic prediction on breaking a resistance level. The presenter also acknowledges that the broader cryptocurrency market is having a bad day and says a weekend shift into crypto is only “a possibility.” That combination is consistent with conditional market commentary: the audience is given uncertainty, price levels, and a scenario to evaluate, not a promise that the coin will produce a fixed return.

citations.quote: why it could be going higher soon
we could possibly see another 10% in gains by the time this video comes out
If it does, this thing could be on a rocket ship.
just a possibility

rebuttal.rebuttal: The title's “EXPLODE” wording is attention-grabbing, but the spoken analysis is materially more conditional: it says “could,” “possibly,” and “if.” The resistance discussion identifies a level to watch; it does not establish that viewers were promised a purchase outcome. Even the cited 10% statement is expressly framed as something that might happen by publication, not as a guaranteed result.

citations.quote: why it could be going higher soon
we could possibly see another 10% in gains by the time this video comes out
If it does, this thing could be on a rocket ship.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Conditional wording does not neutralize the overall promotional message. The title says the coin is “About To EXPLODE,” and the speaker predicts that it could reach the $43 resistance and produce another 10% gain. Those are concrete near-term upside cues, even if phrased with “could” and “possibly”; the quotes do not show a balanced warning about the risk of losing money.

citations.quote: TERRA LUNA Coin Is About To EXPLODE After This!

we could possibly see another 10% in gains by the time this video comes out

opening.argument: The presenter frames the substantive portion as an explanatory review of what Terra is and how its ecosystem works. He asks what viewers are investing in, then describes stablecoins, payment use, synthetic assets, smart contracts, and where to find the white paper and project information. The supplied screens likewise show rankings, social-volume data, project pages, and trading charts, which are materials used to explain a market and technology. The video therefore provides commentary and demonstrations of available information; describing possible price scenarios within that review does not by itself turn the entire presentation into a deceptive solicitation.

citations.quote: what even is Terra Luna coin um like what am I investing in so let's go over that right now
basically it's programmable money for the internet
you can go read their white paper if you want and read these news articles

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution treats chart discussion as solicitation, but the video explicitly transitions into explaining what the asset is and directs viewers to the project's white paper and news articles. The chart and ranking screens support an informational market review. A forecast inside an analysis can remain commentary, especially where the speaker explains resistance and market context rather than instructing viewers to buy a specified amount.

citations.quote: what even is Terra Luna coin um like what am I investing in so let's go over that right now
you can go read their white paper if you want and read these news articles
let's get into some technical analysis

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The explanatory material is secondary to the repeated upside framing. The video opens by asking why LUNA could go higher soon, labels it as “about to explode,” and ends its chart analysis with a rocket-ship prediction if the level breaks. Showing project features or charts does not make those price claims neutral; the cited educational passages do not establish that the speaker warned viewers against speculative participation.

opening.argument: The separate Public mention is an ordinary referral promotion with its condition stated openly: viewers are told they can get “up to 70 dollars” in a free stock when they deposit one dollar, and they are directed to the first description link. The presenter also describes following the channel's portfolio and posts. Nothing in the supplied material shows a guaranteed investment return, a request for credentials, downline income, or a completed transaction. The LUNA discussion itself provides market observations and possible scenarios, but does not show the creator collecting money or claiming that viewers will receive a fixed profit. On this record, the observed promotion is an ordinary app reward, while the financial mechanism alleged is not established.

citations.quote: You can get up to 70 dollars with a free stock when you just deposit one dollar on public
it's going to be the first link in our description
we actually do show a lot of our public stock portfolio as well as our trades on there

rebuttal.rebuttal: The Public offer is visibly a referral-style promotion, but its terms are disclosed as “up to” $70 for a stated one-dollar deposit. That is different from a guaranteed LUNA return or an undisclosed payment demand. The supplied material does not show a completed transaction, a promised profit, or a credential request. The existence of a link and an ordinary reward cannot establish the separate scam mechanism alleged for token appreciation.

citations.quote: You can get up to 70 dollars with a free stock when you just deposit one dollar on public
it's going to be the first link in our description

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Calling the Public offer ordinary does not answer the central LUNA promotion. The speaker directly asks viewers how much LUNA they have and how much they want, then presents near-term upside and a possible 10% gain. The deposit condition also shows an audience-directed financial action, while “up to” qualifies only the app reward; it does not qualify the video's repeated encouragement that LUNA may rise.
